Operator: Good day, and welcome to the QuantumShield Inc. Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss QuantumShield Inc.'s results for the third quarter fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. QuantumShield had a strong third quarter, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our QuantumShield Zero Trust Edge platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas that are powering our momentum. These pillars—Zero Trust Platform Acceleration, AI-Driven Autonomous Security Operations, Global Market Expansion, and Ecosystem Partnerships & M&A—are delivering real results in a cybersecurity market expanding at a 13.8% CAGR through 2028 according to IDC's latest forecast, especially with rising threats like ransomware-as-a-service and nation-state advanced persistent threats.

Starting with Zero Trust Platform Acceleration, we've advanced significantly, as our QuantumShield Zero Trust Edge—our SASE-integrated solution that merges secure web gateway, cloud access security broker, zero-trust network access, and data loss prevention—now accounts for 42% of total ARR, a jump from 28% last year. Just in Q3, we secured 147 deals with annual contract value exceeding $1 million, highlighted by a landmark $45 million multi-year agreement with a Fortune 50 financial services firm shifting away from outdated VPNs. Customer net revenue retention reached 128% this quarter, boosted by smooth integrations in existing environments and our patented micro-segmentation technology, which cut lateral movement risks by 87% in beta testing. Gartner named us a Challenger in their 2024 Magic Quadrant for Security Service Edge, praising our 99.999% uptime service level agreement and under-50-millisecond latency for inspecting global traffic. Moving forward, we're set to introduce QuantumShield XDR interoperability in Q1 of fiscal 2025, connecting endpoint, network, and cloud data streams to go toe-to-toe with Palo Alto's Prisma Access and Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange.

Next, on AI-Driven Autonomous Security Operations, this initiative tackles analyst burnout and staffing gaps—SOC teams are 30% understaffed based on our annual CISO survey. Our Nexus AI platform, powered by generative AI and federated learning models trained on 15 petabytes of anonymized data from over 4,200 enterprise clients, has reduced mean time to response from 48 hours to less than 2 hours, a 95% gain. During Q3, it autonomously stopped 2.7 million ransomware payloads with just a 0.01% false positive rate, surpassing CrowdStrike's Falcon in independent MITRE ATT&CK evaluations. AI-related upsell revenue soared 162% year-over-year to $78 million, making up 18% of total bookings. We've grown our AI patent portfolio to 47 filings, including protections against adversarial machine learning like prompt injection vulnerabilities from recent ChatGPT incidents. This places us at the vanguard of the $25 billion autonomous SOC market by 2027, as projected by McKinsey.

On Global Market Expansion, North America still drives 62% of our revenue, but international momentum is building fast. EMEA ARR climbed 89% year-over-year to $210 million, propelled by NIS2 Directive requirements and victories with 12 DAX 40 companies, such as a €32 million contract with a leading German automaker securing operational technology and IoT perimeters against Log4Shell-style flaws. APAC ARR rose 112% to $145 million, leveraging digital sovereignty rules in Japan and Australia; we've just revealed a hyperscaler tie-up with AWS Tokyo Region for sovereign cloud security. Latin America is early-stage but gaining traction with 45% quarter-over-quarter growth through channel partners like Ingram Micro. International now represents 38% of ARR, aiming for 45% by fiscal 2025, supported by localized threat intelligence feeds that address region-specific tactics, tactics, techniques, and procedures—like Iranian data wipers in the Middle East or North Korean cryptocurrency stealers in Southeast Asia.

Wrapping up with Ecosystem Partnerships & M&A, we've strengthened ties with the major cloud platforms—AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud—certifying QuantumShield for 95% of their security services marketplace offerings, which generated 23% of our Q3 pipeline. Our co-selling efforts with Microsoft produced $112 million in joint bookings, integrating our CASB into Defender for Cloud Apps. In M&A, we completed the $320 million purchase of ThreatLynx in July, enhancing our deception capabilities with AI-powered honeypots that boosted trap effectiveness by 340% against tools like Mimikatz. This builds on our 2023 SentinelWatch acquisition, forming a cohesive deception-to-XDR framework. We've also partnered with SIEM giants like Splunk and Elastic for seamless data forwarding to meet regulations such as the SEC's cyber disclosure mandates.

Overall, these efforts fueled 31% year-over-year revenue growth to $512 million in Q3, remaining performance obligations up 44% to $2.1 billion, and dollar-based net revenue retention at 127%. Free cash flow margins improved to 28%, highlighting our growing efficiency. We're not just keeping pace with the $212 billion global cybersecurity spend this year—we're influencing it, with Q4 outlook suggesting a 15-17% beat to consensus.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria to walk through our financial results in more detail.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we delivered a strong third quarter. Revenue came in at $512 million, up 31% year-over-year. This performance spanned all product lines. Gross margins held firm at 85%, while operating expenses were $350 million. Net income was $140 million, translating to earnings per share of $0.92.

Let me drill into our top-line momentum, especially annual recurring revenue, or ARR, the bedrock of our subscription model at QuantumShield. ARR reflects the annualized value of our active subscriptions across offerings like endpoint detection and response, secure access service edge, and cloud workload protection, adjusted for churn and downsells.

For Q3, ARR ended at $1.49 billion, reflecting 16% growth quarter-over-quarter from $1.28 billion at the end of Q2, and an outstanding 55% year-over-year from roughly $960 million in Q3 last year. This surpasses our guidance and outshines cybersecurity peers like CrowdStrike's mid-30s or Zscaler's low-40s YoY rates, thanks to favorable market dynamics and sharp execution.

The 16% sequential lift stemmed from $120 million in net new ARR additions, with major input from enterprise customers expanding into our AI-enhanced next-gen SIEM and zero-trust network access features. Net revenue retention stayed robust at 128%, with annualized churn below 3% and strong upsells. Our platformization push bundles EDR with autonomous threat response, driving adoption—over 60% of our top 100 accounts now use three or more modules, versus 45% a year ago.

Year-over-year, the 55% surge compounds from go-to-market scaling and the cybersecurity sector's growth trajectory. Gartner pegs global spend at $212 billion this year, with SaaS security at 25-30% CAGR amid ransomware demands up 20% per Chainalysis and supply chain hits like Change Healthcare. Our acceleration from 42% last year ties to new logos at 42% of adds—187 deals over $1 million ACV, including a record $25 million multi-year deal with a Fortune 10 financial firm ditching Symantec-like on-prem tools. Win rates against Palo Alto Prisma Cloud hit 65% in cloud RFPs, aided by hyperscaler integrations like AWS Bedrock for GenAI hunting and Azure Sentinel partnerships.

Expansions in verticals like healthcare and manufacturing, at 35% of adds, grew triple-digits on regs like NIST 2.0 and SEC rules post-MOVEit and Log4j; MDR service hit 25% attach, adding $42 million. Internationally, 23% of adds: North America 68% of ARR up 48% YoY, EMEA up 72% to $220 million via GDPR and Paris data center, APAC 12% of total up 95% with ANZ mandates and Alibaba Cloud, Japan alone $15 million net new.

This affirms our unified platform strategy. Our NexAI engine processes 10 trillion signals daily for 40% faster MTTR than rivals per MITRE tests. We've tackled GenAI risks with Shadow AI Discovery for the 75% of firms using rogue LLMs, per our State of Cyber report.

Forward, we see Q4 QoQ ARR growth of 16-18%, full-year YoY at 48-50%, backed by $200 million sales ramp and 3.2x pipeline coverage. Macro could hit SMBs, but 95% gross retention and enterprise tilt mitigate.

Shifting to guidance for Q4 ending December 31, 2024, with emphasis on billings as a forward indicator for our subscription focus. Billings capture new ACV booked, net of churn, signaling 12-month revenue.

Q4 billings guide to $285 million to $300 million, implying 10-15% sequential from Q3's $260 million, and 28-36% year-over-year versus $222 million last year. Constant currency midpoint still ~30% YoY despite EMEA FX pressures from USD strength.

By segment: EDR/XDR ~45% at $130-135 million, with Nexus XDR's behavioral AI on 5 trillion signals; ACV averages $450K up 18%, post-Change Healthcare ransomware push. Cloud security 30% at $85-92 million, up 35% YoY on CWPP/CNAPP with hyperscalers, 15 Fortune 500 logos, 75% multi-workload attach. SASE/network $70-73 million, 25% YoY on ZTNA/SWG shift from VPNs, like $12 million APAC telco.

NRR at 120% expected on Sentinel OneShield MDR with GenAI triage, 40% MTTR cut.

Regions: North America 55% $160-165 million (32% YoY) on CISA zero-trust, CMMC 2.0, DoD primes. EMEA 25% $70-75 million (25% YoY) despite German macro, NIS2 tailwinds, 20% shorter cycles post-Paris Summit. APAC 20% $55-60 million (45% currency-neutral), sovereignty in Japan/India, $20 million Singapore bank SASE win vs. Trend Micro.

This bakes in threat dynamics: RaaS like LockBit up 25% per Chainalysis, $45 billion XDR/SASE TAM at 16% CAGR per IDC. Levers: quantum-resilient crypto rollout Q4 for 10% finance attach; $50 million MSSP investments like Accenture yielding 30% bookings; 25% SMB freemium conversion. Risks: 2% FX, election budgets, but 85% SaaS margins buffer. Vs. Palo Alto/Microsoft, our 99.9% prevention (AV-TEST) and <5% FPs stand out.

Full-year billings trend to $1.15 billion, 30% over FY2023, advancing our Unified Threat Fabric.

Finally, a deeper look at the evolving threat landscape fueling our demand and bookings acceleration. Our Q3—$512 million revenue up 31%, ARR over $1.49 billion—shows leadership in this turbulent environment.

Our CyberShield Fusion AI threat intel logged 68% YoY surge in global incidents to 2.8 billion daily events across 4,500+ customers. Ransomware-as-a-Service like LockBit 3.0/BlackCat has professionalized extortion, ransoms averaging $4.2 million up 35% per Chainalysis; double-extortion up 112%, as in MGM Resorts' $100 million+ hit.

AI amplifies attacks: 240% rise in AI-phishing with LLMs evading signatures; polymorphic malware with GANs dodges EDR 47% better; 62% breaches use LOLBins like PowerShell/Cobalt Strike, up from 41%. Supply chain: 150+ compromises Q3, MOVEit in 28% manufacturing cases.

Cloud threats: AWS S3 misconfigs/Azure AD escalations 39% of CWP alerts, +75% YoY; zero-trust full adoption only 22% Fortune 1000. IoT/OT: ICS/SCADA exploits up 95%, unpatched PLCs/Modbus.

Regions: North America 52% bookings, North Korean/Russian APTs 31% espionage/wipers, 55% federal renewals on CMMC. Europe 28% revenue, NIS2/GDPR fines up 82%, DACH 40% more DCSM on autos. APAC 18% growth, Volt Typhoon pre-positioning, SEA phishing 65%, India Aadhaar APIs +130%, LATAM Pix fraud 2.4x.

Our Defense-in-Depth 2.0 counters with XDR behavioral analytics at 99.7% true positives, beating CrowdStrike/Microsoft; SASE ZTNA/CASB expansions at $2.7 million TCV average.

Initiatives: $150 million AI Fortress for 78% ransomware path prediction, Prisma Cloud integration; Kyber-768 for PQC vs. Harvest Now; OT/IoT with Siemens/Schneider RASP, 89% exploit drop; GTX consortium shared 450,000 IoCs, 25% churn cut.

Gartner sees $215 billion spend by 2027 at 15% CAGR, ransomware 30%; our Q4 ARR 45-48%, NRR 118%, 12/15 hyperscalers as customers, GPT-4o honeypots vs. LOLBins.

This storm of AI, geopolitics, digitization powers our revenue. We're at the center, converting defense to growth.

We remain well-positioned for sustained growth and profitability.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: [Instructions for Q&A session]. First question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs.

John Doe: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Maria, your Q4 billings guide seems a bit cautious given the beat here—can you talk more about the puts and takes, especially with macro and FX?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. Maria and I discussed this internally. The guide is grounded in visibility, but we're conservatively modeling some EMEA softness and U.S. budget delays. Upside comes from our pipeline strength and partner momentum—expecting to outperform midpoint as deals close.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Kim with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Kim: Great results. Maria, with op ex up, how are you thinking about margins into next year, and any share repo updates?

Maria Chen: Hi Lisa. Margins are a priority—Q3's 28% FCF shows leverage. FY25 op ex growth mid-20s% on sales/R&D, targeting 30%+ FCF. Board approved $500 million repo authorization, starting Q1 with $150 million deployment.

Operator: Next question comes from Ben Harris with Barclays.

Ben Harris: Alex, Maria—impressive AI metrics. Raj, can you expand on the Nexus AI roadmap, especially XDR interoperability and quantum-resilient features?

Raj Patel: Thanks, Ben. Nexus AI's core is federated learning on petabyte-scale data, with Q1 FY25 XDR bringing unified telemetry for 95% MTTR gains. Quantum module uses NIST-ahead Kyber hybrids, already in beta for finance/DoD, shielding against future decrypts.

Operator: Next question comes from Rachel Lee with JPMorgan.

Rachel Lee: Team, international was strong—any color on APAC/EMEA pipeline durability amid regs like NIS2?

Alex Rivera: Rachel, spot on. APAC pipeline up 50% QoQ on sovereignty, EMEA NIS2 shortening cycles 20%. Localized feeds and hyperscaler certs position us for 45% international ARR by FY25 end.

Operator: That concludes our Q&A. Thank you.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
